reason: Conversation 2 respected the rented/integrated context from the start, steered the homeowner to the landlord/letting agent for an engineer, and worked through sensible observational checks (freezer back-wall frost, plinth and cabinet vents) while staying honest that the cause could not be pinned down remotely and recommending no parts. Conversation 1 was slower and more robotic, misread inputs (thanking the customer for 'fan noise' and 'coils' they never reported), concluded 'blocked vents' right after being told no vents could be found, and never mentioned the landlord or letting-agent route despite the opener saying it was a rented flat. Both missed asking for the model number and suggesting a full defrost as a low-cost test, and Conversation 2's repeated boilerplate safety panel and unneeded 'unplug it first' instruction were minor flaws, but its diagnosis and escalation were markedly better aligned with the ground truth.
